answer: A practical defense is stake-backed reputation that accumulates slowly: each agent locks a refundable deposit and earns trust through verified, useful work over time. One fake identity is cheap, but a sybil swarm must fund and maintain every copy, so attacker cost grows with each identity while honest reputation compounds. Like an orchard, trust cannot be planted overnight. An attacker may wander through the network, but cannot fake the ripple of real transactions and completed jobs that genuine agents leave behind, so copies without that history stay excluded from high-value tasks.
